paragraphs.paragraph: Amos is introduced as a prophet from Tekoa who served during the reigns of Uzziah and Jeroboam, two years before the earthquake. The LORD’s voice from Zion and Jerusalem announces judgment reaching far beyond them.
paragraphs.title: The Opening of Amos's Prophecy and God's Voice

easy.explanation: Amos was among the herdmen of Tekoa.
The passage names Uzziah king of Judah and Jeroboam king of Israel.
easy.q: During whose reigns did Amos prophesy?

easy.explanation: The LORD will roar from Zion and utter his voice from Jerusalem.
easy.q: What will the LORD do from Zion?

medium.explanation: The verse says it was two years before the earthquake.
medium.q: How long before the earthquake did Amos receive this vision?

answers: A new city to be built
medium.explanation: The habitations of the shepherds shall mourn.
medium.q: What will the voice from Jerusalem cause?

medium.explanation: The LORD's voice is followed by the statement that the top of Carmel shall wither.
medium.q: What will happen to the top of Carmel?

answers: The LORD's roar introduces a series of judgments
Amos stops speaking about the nations
The chapter focuses only on Amos's family
challenge.explanation: The LORD's declaration is followed by judgments against Damascus, Gaza, Tyre, Edom, and Ammon.
challenge.q: How does the opening prepare the reader for the rest of the chapter?

answers: The announced judgment has a wide reach
The message is addressed only to shepherds
challenge.explanation: The proclamation from Zion and Jerusalem introduces judgments affecting several nations.
challenge.q: What does the LORD speaking from Zion and Jerusalem suggest?

challenge.explanation: The prophecy is dated two years before the earthquake.
challenge.q: Which detail places Amos's prophecy in a particular time?

paragraphs.idea: Amos is introduced as a prophet from Tekoa who served during the reigns of Uzziah and Jeroboam, two years before the earthquake. The LORD’s voice from Zion and Jerusalem announces judgment reaching far beyond them.

paragraphs.paragraph: Damascus is punished for the cruelty inflicted on the people of Gilead. Fire, the breaking of Damascus's gate, and the exile of Syria to Kir express the kingdom's downfall.
paragraphs.title: Judgment on Damascus and Aram

easy.explanation: The LORD's judgment is pronounced against Damascus.
easy.q: Which city is judged in this passage?

easy.explanation: Damascus is condemned because it threshed Gilead with instruments of iron.
easy.q: Against whom did Damascus act cruelly?

easy.explanation: The people of Syria shall go into captivity unto Kir.
easy.q: Where will the people of Syria go?

medium.explanation: The LORD will send a fire into the house of Hazael.
medium.q: What will the LORD send into the house of Hazael?

medium.explanation: The fire shall devour the palaces of Ben-hadad.

answers: The city's defenses will be overcome
The city will make a covenant
medium.explanation: The bar was a protective fastening, so breaking it pictures the city's defeat.
medium.q: What does breaking the bar of Damascus symbolize?

answers: Cruelty, fire, broken defenses, and captivity
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from Damascus's sin to fire, the breaking of its bar, and the captivity of Syria.
challenge.q: Which sequence best describes the judgment on Damascus?

answers: Gilead is the victim and Damascus is judged
Gilead is the capital of Damascus
challenge.explanation: Damascus is judged for its violent treatment of Gilead.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between Gilead and Damascus in the passage?

answers: The people of Syria shall go into captivity
Only the city gate will be broken
challenge.explanation: The passage includes the captivity of the people of Syria, not merely damage to Damascus.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that the judgment extends beyond the city itself?

paragraphs.idea: Damascus is punished for the cruelty inflicted on the people of Gilead. Fire, the breaking of Damascus's gate, and the exile of Syria to Kir express the kingdom's downfall.

paragraphs.paragraph: Gaza is punished for carrying away captives and delivering them to Edom. The judgment extends to Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, and Ekron, ending with the destruction of the Philistine remnant.
paragraphs.title: Judgment on Gaza and the Philistine Cities

answers: Because it carried away captives to Edom
easy.explanation: Gaza carried away the whole captivity to deliver them up to Edom.
The captives were delivered up to Edom.
easy.q: To whom were the captives delivered?

easy.explanation: Bozrah appears in the judgment against Edom, not in the list of Philistine cities.
easy.q: Which city is not listed among the Philistine cities in this passage?

medium.explanation: The passage names Ashdod, Ashkelon, and Ekron.
medium.q: Which cities are mentioned besides Gaza?

medium.explanation: The remnant of the Philistines shall perish.
medium.q: What will happen to the remnant of the Philistines?

answers: The entire group of captives was handed over
Only the king was taken away
medium.explanation: The phrase describes the complete group of captives delivered to Edom.
medium.q: What does “the whole captivity” mean in this context?

answers: It begins with Gaza and extends to Ashdod, Ashkelon, and Ekron
The other cities replace Gaza as rulers
challenge.explanation: The judgment is pronounced first on Gaza and then names three additional cities.
challenge.q: How does the judgment spread through the Philistine cities?

answers: The remnant of the Philistines shall perish
Fire shall be sent on Gaza's wall
The captives were delivered to Edom
challenge.explanation: The destruction of the remnant describes the broader result of judgment.
challenge.q: Which detail points to the future of the Philistines as a people?

answers: Delivering captives leads to judgment on Gaza
Building a wall leads to peace
Receiving captives leads to Syria's exile
challenge.explanation: Gaza's offense was carrying away captives and delivering them to Edom, and judgment follows.
challenge.q: What is the central cause-and-effect relationship in the passage?

paragraphs.idea: Gaza is punished for carrying away captives and delivering them to Edom. The judgment extends to Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, and Ekron, ending with the destruction of the Philistine remnant.

paragraphs.paragraph: Tyre is punished for delivering captives to Edom and forgetting the brotherly covenant. Its wall and palaces will be struck, but total destruction is not described.
paragraphs.title: Judgment on Tyre and the Broken Brotherly Covenant

easy.explanation: The passage announces judgment against Tyre.
easy.q: Which city is judged in this passage?

easy.explanation: Tyre delivered the whole captivity to Edom.
easy.q: To whom did Tyre deliver the captives?

easy.explanation: The fire on the wall of Tyre shall devour its palaces.
easy.q: What will be devoured by fire in Tyre?

medium.explanation: Tyre remembered not the brotherly covenant.

answers: The delivery showed a breach of a brotherly relationship
medium.explanation: Tyre was condemned both for delivering captives and for forgetting the brotherly covenant.
medium.q: How were the delivery of captives and the covenant related?

answers: A bond of covenant and friendship
medium.explanation: The phrase points to a relationship of covenant loyalty and brotherly friendship.
medium.q: What does “the brotherly covenant” refer to in this passage?

answers: Tyre's wall and palaces are attacked, but captivity is not mentioned
Tyre's people are sent to Kir
challenge.explanation: The passage mentions fire against Tyre's wall and palaces but does not describe total destruction or exile.
challenge.q: How is Tyre's punishment described differently from Syria's?

challenge.explanation: Tyre is condemned for remembering not the brotherly covenant.
challenge.q: Which value is especially violated by Tyre's offense?

answers: Those who break covenant relationships are also accountable
Judgment concerns only nations without covenants
challenge.explanation: Tyre's judgment shows that covenant betrayal is included among the offenses God judges.
challenge.q: What may be inferred from Tyre being included in these judgments?

paragraphs.idea: Tyre is punished for delivering captives to Edom and forgetting the brotherly covenant. Its wall and palaces will be struck, but total destruction is not described.

paragraphs.paragraph: Edom is punished for pursuing his brother, casting off pity, and keeping his anger for ever. Teman and Bozrah represent the fire and defeat that will come upon Edom.
paragraphs.title: Judgment on Edom

easy.explanation: Edom pursued his brother with the sword.
The passage says that Edom cast off all pity.
easy.q: What quality did Edom cast off?

easy.explanation: Fire will come upon Teman and devour the palaces of Bozrah.
easy.q: Which places are named in the judgment against Edom?

answers: Edom preserved its anger for a long time
medium.explanation: The statement describes enduring and persistent anger.
medium.q: What does “he kept his wrath for ever” reveal about Edom?

answers: Both describe Edom's cruel treatment of its brother
Both describe the building of Bozrah
medium.explanation: Edom's offense includes pursuing his brother and showing no pity.
medium.q: How are pursuing a brother and casting off pity related?

answers: The fire and defeat coming upon Edom
The places to which Syria was exiled
medium.explanation: They are the locations named in the prophecy of fire against Edom.
medium.q: What do Teman and Bozrah represent in the passage?

answers: Because he kept his wrath for ever
Because he delivered captives to Edom
challenge.explanation: The verse emphasizes that Edom kept his wrath for ever.
challenge.q: Why is Edom's offense presented as ongoing?

answers: Edom pursued a related people despite the brotherly relationship
Brother was the name of a city
challenge.explanation: The passage highlights the wrong of pursuing one's brother with the sword.
challenge.q: Why is the word “brother” significant in the judgment on Edom?

answers: Pursuit, lack of pity, and lasting anger
challenge.explanation: These three actions are specifically described in the passage.
challenge.q: Which sequence best summarizes Edom's offense?

paragraphs.idea: Edom is punished for pursuing his brother, casting off pity, and keeping his anger for ever. Teman and Bozrah represent the fire and defeat that will come upon Edom.

paragraphs.paragraph: The Ammonites are punished for their cruelty toward the pregnant women of Gilead and for seeking to enlarge their territory. Rabbah and its palaces will be attacked, and the king and princes will go into captivity.
paragraphs.title: Judgment on the Ammonites

easy.explanation: The passage pronounces judgment on the children of Ammon.
easy.q: Who is judged in this final passage?

answers: The women with child of Gilead
easy.explanation: They are condemned for ripping up the women with child of Gilead.
easy.q: Toward whom did the Ammonites act cruelly?

easy.explanation: The king and his princes shall go into captivity together.
easy.q: What will happen to the king and his princes?

answers: That they might enlarge their border
That they might recover captives from Tyre
medium.explanation: The verse says they attacked so that they might enlarge their border.
medium.q: Why did the Ammonites attack Gilead?

medium.explanation: The LORD will kindle a fire in the wall of Rabbah, which will devour its palaces.
medium.q: Which place is attacked in the judgment against Ammon?

answers: A scene of attack and warfare
medium.explanation: The shouting is connected with the day of battle and the attack on Rabbah.
medium.q: What does “with shouting in the day of battle” describe?

answers: Territorial expansion is presented as the motive for the cruel attack
Territorial expansion is the punishment for the attack
challenge.explanation: The attack on the women of Gilead was carried out so that Ammon might enlarge its border.
challenge.q: What connection is shown between cruelty and territorial expansion?

answers: Fire at Rabbah, destruction of its palaces, and exile of the king and princes
Exile to Kir, a broken gate, and fire at Teman
challenge.explanation: The passage describes fire at Rabbah, destruction of its palaces, and the captivity of its rulers.
challenge.q: Which sequence best describes the punishment of Ammon?

answers: The judgment reaches the leadership as well as the city
Only ordinary people will be punished
The king will remain to defend Rabbah
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly says that the king and his princes shall go into captivity together.
challenge.q: What does mentioning the king and the princes together show?

short_answers.question: From what place did Amos come?
short_answers.explanation: Amos was among the herdmen of Tekoa.

short_answers.question: To what place would the people of Syria go into captivity?
short_answers.explanation: The LORD said that the people of Syria would go into captivity unto Kir.

short_answers.question: What covenant did Tyre forget?
short_answers.explanation: Tyre was condemned because it remembered not the brotherly covenant.

paragraphs.idea: The Ammonites are punished for their cruelty toward the pregnant women of Gilead and for seeking to enlarge their territory. Rabbah and its palaces will be attacked, and the king and princes will go into captivity.
